profileName: AI EdTech — Conceptual Clarity, Persuasion & Functional Spoken English (B2)

watchOuts.tag: Functional Speech · Moving From Careful Detail to Spoken Flow
watchOuts.title: Keep Sentences Tight and Functional So Logic Lands in Live Conversation
watchOuts.detail: At B2, building detailed, logical explanations is a real strength—but long, multi-clause sentences can slow down everyday peer talk or get lost in fast discussions. State one clear premise at a time, use clean connectors ('so', 'which means', 'for example'), and check in with your listener.

watchOuts.tag: Conceptual Clarity · Explaining Complex Ideas Simply
watchOuts.title: Anchor Abstract EdTech and Ethics Ideas in Concrete Classroom Examples
watchOuts.detail: Teaching 6th-grade science and 3rd/4th-grade ethics already trains you to make big ideas understandable to young minds. Carry that same clarity into adult conversations: define the core concept in plain words before adding detail or nuance.

watchOuts.tag: Persuasion With Trust · Pairing Logic With Empathy
watchOuts.title: Lead With Shared Human Value Before Making a Logical Case
watchOuts.detail: Strong logic can feel cold or rigid if you jump straight to arguments before establishing empathy and trust. Show why a learner, teacher, or teammate matters first—then lay out your reasoning step by step.

watchOuts.tag: Korean L1 Spoken Habits · Rhythm, Articles, and Directness
watchOuts.title: Watch Article Choices, Subject-Verb Directness, and Pauses in Speech
watchOuts.detail: In spoken English, missing articles ('a/an/the') or starting with long background clauses before the main point can make clear thoughts sound tentative. Put your main point early and pause briefly rather than rushing through complex ideas.

watchOuts.tag: Seoul to Canada Transition · Adapting Tone Across Cultures
watchOuts.title: Balance Thoughtful Depth With Open, Conversational Peer Dialogue
watchOuts.detail: As you prepare for peer interactions and a potential move to Canada, treat conversations as collaborative back-and-forth rather than a lecture. Share your structured view, then invite peers' reactions openly.

scenarios.title: Peer Conversation: Connecting Elementary Teaching to AI EdTech
scenarios.prompt: Talk with a peer about what teaching 6th-grade science and 3rd/4th-grade ethics taught you about how people learn—and how that shapes your thinking on AI in education. Keep your explanation clear, logical, and conversational.

scenarios.title: Persuading With Logic and Empathy: Why AI Should Support, Not Replace, Care
scenarios.prompt: Make a persuasive case to a colleague or startup collaborator about why AI edtech must protect human connection, trust, and the value of life. Start with a concrete human concern, then give two logical reasons why it matters.

scenarios.title: Breaking Down a Concept Simply: Explaining a Detailed Idea in 45 Seconds
scenarios.prompt: Explain a detailed idea—such as how students build real understanding versus memorizing steps—in plain, spoken English without jargon. Make sure the main takeaway is obvious right away.

scenarios.title: Navigating a Shift to Canada: Peer Check-In on Goals and Growth
scenarios.prompt: Have a natural, everyday conversation with a peer about preparing for life and work in Canada—what excites you, what feels uncertain, and what kind of leadership you want to grow into.

scenarios.title: Building Trust in a Team: Handling a Disagreement Constructively
scenarios.prompt: A peer disagrees with your logical plan for a learning tool. Respond with empathy first, show you heard their concern accurately, and walk through your reasoning calmly so trust stays intact.

customCards.term: Conceptual Clarity Frame: Start with the core idea in one simple line before adding details.
customCards.definition: "Here's the core idea in plain terms: technology works best when it helps learners think for themselves, not just get faster answers."
customCards.example: Naming the central claim up front keeps detailed explanations easy to follow.
customCards.note: Conceptual Clarity: Simple framing makes complex logic effortless to grasp.

customCards.term: Empathy + Logic Bridge: Link human care directly to your logical reasoning.
customCards.definition: "Students only open up when they feel safe and respected. That's why any AI tool in a classroom has to build trust first."
customCards.example: Connecting values and cause-and-effect makes your argument feel both thoughtful and practical.
customCards.note: Persuasion & Trust: Logic persuades faster when it rests on shared human care.

customCards.term: Functional Speech Trim: Break a dense, multi-part thought into two short, spoken sentences.
customCards.definition: "Instead of 'Because in elementary school students need concrete examples to understand abstract rules, if an AI skips that step they get confused,' say: 'Young learners need concrete examples before abstract rules. If AI skips that step, they get confused.'"
customCards.example: Shorter sentences keep your logic sharp and easy to hear in live conversation.
customCards.note: Functional English: Crisp sentences beat long, winding clauses in spoken dialogue.

customCards.term: Persuasion Check-In: Invite peer perspective after making a clear point.
customCards.definition: "That's how I see the learning side of it—how does that line up with what you're seeing?"
customCards.example: Turning a point into an open question builds strong peer rapport and trust.
customCards.note: Peer Interaction & Leadership: Collaborative framing invites genuine dialogue.

customCards.term: Beachcombing Drill ('Ethics Card' / 'Purpose'): Ground a leadership idea in everyday values.
customCards.definition: "In 3rd-grade ethics, kids ask 'Is this fair?' In AI edtech, the deeper question is 'Does this respect human growth and the value of life?'"
customCards.example: Drawing from real teaching moments gives your startup vision authenticity.
customCards.note: Beachcombing & Value of Life: Concrete roots keep big goals grounded.

customCards.term: Canada & Peer Transition: Express near-term curiosity and long-term ambition naturally.
customCards.definition: "Right now I'm focused on connecting with peers and sharpening how I explain ideas in English, while building toward leading an AI edtech team."
customCards.example: Stating your near-term step and long-term direction clearly makes your path easy to support.
customCards.note: Functional Speech & Direction: Clear near-term vs. long-term framing builds credibility.
